topics.label: Lecture Introduction and Learning Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecturer, outlines the scope of the lecture on cancer causation, and presents the key learning objectives.

topics.label: Origins and Etiology of Cancer: Intrinsic Mutagenesis, Genetics, and Environment
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish the conceptual framework of cancer etiology by exploring how intrinsic cellular mutations, genetic predisposition, and environmental exposures interact to drive cancer development across populations.

topics.label: Biological, Chemical, and Physical Carcinogens and Mechanisms of Carcinogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics investigate specific biological, chemical, and physical carcinogens to illustrate the diverse molecular and microenvironmental mechanisms underlying tumor initiation, promotion, and tissue vulnerability.

topics.label: Methodologies for Identifying Mutagens and Determining Carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe the genomic, epidemiological, in vivo, and in vitro methodologies used to detect mutagenic damage and determine the carcinogenicity of various agents.

topics.label: Lecture Summary and Risk-Benefit Analysis
topics.groupedBecause: This closing subtopic summarizes the main themes of the lecture and considers the practical balance between environmental cancer risks and daily benefits.
